C1.rationale: Level 1, not 2 (demoted on review): the only textual link between the assessed Practice Portfolio (PHTY90114, 20%) and the Collaborator outcome ('collaborate with colleagues from other disciplines in the evolution of management plans') is the generic catch-all clause 'advanced clinical reasoning and achievement of all learning outcomes set for the subject' in the subject overview — not a specific description of a graded task that assesses interdisciplinary coordination. An outcome stated but not clearly and specifically tied to a graded task is not evidence of assessed attainment; per the rubric's ambiguity-resolves-down rule, L1 is at least as defensible as L2 on this record.
evidenceLines: Effectively demonstrate advanced expertise as a clinician in interdisciplinary contexts and collaborate with colleagues from other disciplines in the evolution of management plans

They will employ multiple learning strategies to complete a Practice Portfolio that will show evidence of: highly developed clinical expertise as judged by senior clinicians; completion of online modules; mentoring and educating junior and peer clinicians; role modelling; advanced clinical reasoning and achievement of all learning outcomes set for the subject.
Professional portfolio, collected throughout the subject

C2.rationale: Anchor (L2): criterion-referenced appraisal of quality (peer review/structured critique). PHTY90114's video-based Peer report and REHB90010's Critical Appraisal of Research (30%) satisfy L2. No documented reliance-decision justification or process-focused strategy-adjustment assessment for L3.
evidenceLines: Peer report (based on observation of a video of clinical practice), due throughout the study period as determined by the student
Critical Appraisal of Research
Critically appraise experimental studies, including clinical trials as well as systematic reviews and synthesize their application to contemporary clinical practice.

C3.rationale: Anchor (L1): AI/digital tools appear only as electives. Core (compulsory + capstone) subjects contain no digital/AI content; REHB90009 and RADI90024, both electives, exactly match the L1 anchor.
evidenceLines: This subject will introduce students to innovative and contemporary technology that has been recently developed and is currently used in clinical practice and research for the purposes of measurement, diagnosis and prescription.

Students will critically appraise selected innovation and emerging technologies using a scientific approach in order to consolidate their understanding of the key elements that determine feasibility, safety and utility.

C4.rationale: Anchor (L2): application to novel/cross-context problems. REHB90012 (needs assessment + designed program in own practice context) and REHB90013 (hypothesis-testing/dataset-analysis routes) satisfy L2. L3's self-scoped-capstone or own-knowledge-gap route is ambiguous (mentor-guided scoping; needs analysis targets the service context, not personal knowledge gaps), so resolved down.
evidenceLines: Students will conduct a professional project based on a needs assessment within their professional practice context, identifying and justifying priority service areas. Selecting a priority area in collaboration with an academic and professional mentor they will design, justify and present a program, service or resource, including a business case, to address the identified area of need and design a project to meet this need.
Professional Development Portfolio Part 2: Needs analysis report
The research question can be answered by a systematic review of the literature, by an analysis of an existing data set or by testing a hypothesis within an existing research project.

C5.rationale: Anchor (L1): introductory methods unit/proposal assessment. Compulsory REHB90010 caps at a Research proposal (40%). The optional REHB90013 capstone could reach L2 for some students, but primary-evidence generation is only one of three routes within an optional, alternative capstone, so resolved to the compulsory-core floor.
evidenceLines: Research and evidence informs best practice and innovation in health care. This subject will provide graduates with an opportunity to extend their understanding of evidence based practice and research methodology, including research ethics.
Research proposal

This subject is an opportunity for students to integrate knowledge and research skills to define and address a research question. The research question can be answered by a systematic review of the literature, by an analysis of an existing data set or by testing a hypothesis within an existing research project.

W1.rationale: Anchor (L2): professional-genre/beyond-teaching-team assessment judged against practice criteria. PHTY90114's Supervisor Reports (based on observed practice) and its 'accountability to clients, society and the profession' outcome satisfy L2. L3's explicit professional-genre and 'real external audience' requirements are not clearly documented, so resolved down.
evidenceLines: Supervisor Report A and Supervisor Report B (both based on observation of student practice, 10% each, 20 hours of practice x 2) due throughout the study period as determined by the student
Demonstrate accountability to clients, society and responsibility for the profession
Adapt communication to meet evolving situational needs of clients, carers and colleagues

W2.rationale: Level 2, not 3 (demoted on review): the L3 claim that authentic-task assessment forms 'the program's assessment spine ... AND a genuine constraint of practice' relied on evidence that breaks the one-construct-one-home rule and on a capstone that is not guaranteed to every student. The PHTY90030 clinical-placement lines ('two-week clinical placement block ... Royal Children's Hospital', 'prepare a case study for presentation') are workplace-immersion evidence that belongs to W3, where this same submission also cites them as primary evidence — using them a second time here to supply W2's real-patient constraint double-counts a single piece of evidence. REHB90012's business-case capstone is one of two alternative Core Capstone subjects (REHB90012 or REHB90013, 25cp, student's choice) and is not guaranteed core — this submission's own C5 rationale treats the identical choice as 'an optional, alternative capstone' and resolves C5 down for that reason, but W2 had relied on REHB90012 without the same caution. Once the double-counted placement evidence and the non-guaranteed capstone are set aside, only PHTY90114's Practice Portfolio and Clinical Examination — judged by senior clinicians, time-bound to a 6-month completion window — reliably delivers an authentic professional task to every student: a single instance, not the assessment spine L3 requires. Resolved down to L2 per the rubric's ambiguity-resolves-down rule.
evidenceLines: Perform paediatric physiotherapy competencies at a high level accepted by the profession

Students will have 6 months from the time of enrolment to complete all subject intended learning outcomes and assessment tasks, including a clinical examination to a satisfactory standard that demonstrates a high level of competency in their clinical practice.

W3.rationale: Anchor (L2): placement/practicum with supervision and assessment, but short or standalone. PHTY90030's 'two-week clinical placement block' matches this exactly, with assessed continuous clinical assessment and a reflective clinical practice journal. PHTY90114's added 40-hour supervised-practice component could support an L3 required sequence, but its status as a workplace placement (versus supervised assessment of existing practice) is not clearly established, so resolved down.
evidenceLines: Students have a two-week clinical placement block which may include attending the Royal Children's Hospital or associated clinics in Melbourne.
Continuous clinical assessment
Clinical practice journal
Supervisor Report A and Supervisor Report B (both based on observation of student practice, 10% each, 20 hours of practice x 2) due throughout the study period as determined by the student

G1.rationale: Coherent specialist paediatric-physiotherapy core: 75cp of compulsory, discipline-specific subjects, explicitly targeted at physiotherapists specialising in this clinical stream.
evidenceLines: The Master of Physiotherapy (Paediatrics) is designed to produce graduates with advanced knowledge and skills for professional practice in Paediatrics. It is targeted toward early and mid-career physiotherapists who wish to further their careers within this clinical interest stream of physiotherapy practice.
Completion of 75 credit points of Compulsory subjects

G2.rationale: Assessed, accountable clinical decision-making under real uncertainty (adverse-event analysis, risk/benefit weighing, clinical reasoning) within supervised real practice.
evidenceLines: Analyse adverse events and considers the risks and benefits of all assessment and intervention methods, prioritizing and predicting modifications as required when working with clients with complex conditions
Display critical decision-making and clinical reasoning skills for the management of paediatric conditions
Demonstrate advanced clinical decision making and perform therapeutic interventions in a skillful and safe manner, adapting to changing clinical circumstances

ambiguities: C4: REHB90012's needs assessment targets the practice/service context, not the student's own knowledge gaps, and the capstone priority area is mentor-guided rather than independently self-scoped — L3 ('self-scoped capstone' or 'own knowledge gaps + plan') is plausible but not cleanly documented; resolved to L2.

C5: REHB90013 (one of two alternative capstones) could reach L2 conducted-inquiry evidence, but primary-evidence generation is only one of three offered routes within it, and the compulsory REHB90010 only reaches proposal-writing (L1); resolved to L1.

W1: PHTY90114's Supervisor Reports and Professional/Communicator outcomes are practitioner-judged and recur with PHTY90030's placement assessment, which could support L3, but the extract never names a specific professional genre or states explicitly that the audience is 'real and external' beyond placement supervision; resolved to L2.

W3: PHTY90030 (2-week placement) alone matches L2's 'short or stands alone' wording exactly; combined with PHTY90114's 40-hour supervised-practice component it could form an L3 'required sequence... in the core', but the extract does not clearly establish PHTY90114's component as a workplace placement in the same sense as PHTY90030's hospital placement; resolved to L2.

C1: REHB90013's 'part of a research team... in collaboration with an experienced researcher' language was considered as possible additional C1 evidence but the subject's assessed items (individual reports) do not tie collaboration to an explicit assessed criterion, so it was not used to push C1 toward recurrence/Level 3.

C1 (adversarial review): demoted from L2 to L1 because the Practice Portfolio's only stated tie to the Collaborator outcome is the subject's generic 'achievement of all learning outcomes' clause, not a specific graded-task description of interdisciplinary coordination.

W2 (adversarial review): demoted from L3 to L2 because the L3 claim double-counted the PHTY90030 placement (which is W3's evidence) and relied on REHB90012, a non-guaranteed alternative capstone; only PHTY90114 reliably supplies an authentic professional task to every student, which is a single instance rather than an assessment spine.
